title: Prefix-free list encoding
statement: Let $A$ be a type, and let $f$ assign a finite Boolean string to each element of $A$. Suppose $f$ is prefix-free in the strong sense that whenever $f(a)$ followed by a string $s$ equals $f(b)$ followed by a string $t$, one has $a=b$ and $s=t$. Then the encoding of finite lists formed from $f$ is also prefix-free in this sense.
